text_blocks.snippet: The two main types of cholesterol are LDL and HDL. LDL, or low-density lipoprotein, is often called the "bad" cholesterol because high levels can lead to plaque buildup in arteries, increasing the risk of heart disease and stroke. HDL, or high-density lipoprotein, is considered the "good" cholesterol because it helps remove LDL from the arteries and transport it back to the liver for removal from the body.

list.snippet: This type of cholesterol is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. High levels of LDL can cause plaque to build up in the arteries, narrowing them and potentially leading to heart attack or stroke.

list.title: HDL (High-Density Lipoprotein):
list.snippet: This type of cholesterol is beneficial for heart health. HDL helps remove LDL from the arteries, preventing plaque buildup and reducing the risk of cardiovascular problems.

text_blocks.snippet: Understanding the roles of LDL and HDL is crucial for maintaining good cardiovascular health.
